title: Conjecture
body_md: For any fixed prime power $q$, there does not exist an infinite family of cyclic codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with both constant relative distance and constant relative dual distance.

label: prop:primitive
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:primitive}
Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $k$ be a prime so that $q$ is a primitive root modulo $k$.  Then the polynomial $p_k(x):=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}x^i$ is an irreducible polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_q$.

label: fact:cyclic_dual
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fact:cyclic_dual}
Let $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}^n$ be a cyclic code of dimension $k$ with check polynomial $h(x) \in \mathbb{F}_{\leq k}[x]$. Then $C^\perp$ is a cyclic code with generator polynomial  $h^{\mathrm{rev}}(x)$.

label: fact:rm
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fact:rm}
The Reed-Muller code $\mathrm{RM}(r,m)$ has distance $2^{m-r}$, and is  decodable up to half the minimum distance in time $\mathrm{poly}(2^m)$. Moreover, $\mathrm{RM}(r,m)^\perp = \mathrm{RM}(m-r-1,m)$.
head: environment

label: prop:prm
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:prm}
Let $m,r$ be positive integers, let
$\varphi: \mathbb{F}_{2^m} \to \mathbb{F}_2^m$ be an $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear bijection, and let $\alpha$ be a generator of the multiplicative group of the field $\mathbb{F}_{2^m}$. Then the punctured RM code 
$\mathrm{RM}^*(r,m)$ is cyclic when the  evaluation points are ordered as $\varphi(\alpha^i)$ for $i=0,1, \ldots, 2^m-1$.

label: def:sidon
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:sidon}
Let $S=\{s_1,s_2,\dots ,s_d\} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$  be a subset of $d$ distinct integers.
We say that $S$ is a  \textsf{Sidon set} if 
its pairwise differences are all distinct, that is, for any $i,j,k,\ell\in [d]$ so that $i\neq j$ and $k\neq \ell$, it holds that $s_i-s_j=s_k-s_\ell$ if and only if $i=k$ and $j=\ell$.
head: environment
name: Sidon set

label: def:balanced_weight
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:balanced_weight}
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a finite field. 
We define the \textsf{balanced weight} $\mathrm{wt}_\mathrm{bal}(w)$ of a string $w \in \mathbb{F}^n$ as $\min_{\alpha \in \mathbb{F}} |\{i \in [n] \mid w_i \neq \alpha\}|$. Note that $\mathrm{wt}_\mathrm{bal}(w) \geq d$ if any element $\alpha \in \mathbb{F}$ appears at most $n-d$ times in $w$, and that $\mathrm{wt}(w) \geq \mathrm{wt}_\mathrm{bal}(w)$. 
We say that a code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}^k$ is $d$-\textsf{balanced} if $\mathrm{wt}_\mathrm{bal}(c) \geq d$ for any non-zero codeword $c$. 
For an integer $t \geq 2$, we say  that a code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}^{t \cdot k}$ is $(t,d)$-\textsf{balanced} if for any non-zero codeword $c=(c_0, c_1, \ldots,c_{t-1} ) \in C$, where $c_0, c_1, \ldots, c_{t-1} \in \mathbb{F}^k$, we have that $\mathrm{wt}(c_0)+\sum_{i=1}^{t-1}\mathrm{wt}_\mathrm{bal}(c_i) \geq d$.

name: Balanced weight

label: thm:Sidon_to_DC
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Sidon_to_DC}
Suppose that there exists an explicit construction of an infinite sequence of sets $\mathcal{S}=\{S_k\}_{k \in I}$, where $S_k \subseteq [k]$ is a Sidon set of size $d=d(k)$.
 
Then for any prime power $q$, there exists an explicit family of codes $\mathcal{D}=\{D_k\}_{k\in I}$, where $D_k \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^{2 k}$ is a  double-circulant code of distance at least $\frac d 2+1$ that can be decoded from less than $\frac d 4$ errors in time $\mathrm{poly}(k, \log q)$.
Moreover, $D_k$
is $(2,d')$-balanced for $d'=\min\{\frac {d} {2}+1, \frac{k} {d}\}$.

title: Definition
body_md:
We say that a matrix $A$ over a field $\mathbb{F}$ is a
$(d,b)$-\textsf{design matrix} if each column of $A$ has weight at least $d$, and the intersection of the supports of any pair of columns of $A$ has size at most $b$.
head: environment
name: Design matrix

label: lem:sidon_1
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $c=(c_0,c_1) \in C$ be a non-zero codeword, where $c_0, c_1 \in \mathbb{F}_q^k$, we shall show that $wt(c) \geq \frac{d} {b} +1$. To see this, note that $c$ is a non-zero linear combination of columns of $G$. Suppose that this linear combination has $\ell$ non-zero entries $i_1, \ldots, i_\ell \in [k]$ for some $\ell \in [k]$.

Then by the structure of $G$, we have that $\mathrm{wt}(c_0) = \ell$. Moreover, since $A$ is a $(d,b)$-design matrix, we have that the $i_1$ column of $G$ has weight at least $d$, and the support of any other column from $i_2, \ldots, i_\ell$ intersects the support of $i_1$ in at most $b$ entries. Consequently, we have that $\mathrm{wt}(c_1) \geq \max\{0,d - (\ell-1) \cdot b\}$. But this implies in turn that 
$$\mathrm{wt}(c) \geq \ell+ \max\{0,d - (\ell-1) \cdot b\} =\max\{\ell,d +b - \ell(b-1)\} .$$
Finally, note that the righthand expression is minimized when $\ell = \frac{d} {b}+1$, in which case it equals $\frac{d} {b}+1$. 

For the moreover part, 
let $a \in \mathbb{F}_q^k$ denote the first column of $A$, and note that since $A$ is circulant, $\mathrm{wt}(a) \leq r$. Let $c=(c_0,c_1) \in C$ be a non-zero codeword, where $c_0, c_1 \in \mathbb{F}_q^k$. 
Then by Claim \ref{clm:circulant} and the structure of $G$, we have that $c_1$ is the length $k$ coefficient vector of $a(x) \cdot c_0(x) \; (\bmod\; x^k -1)$. Suppose that $\mathrm{wt}(c_0)=\ell$. Then 
$\mathrm{wt}(c_1) \leq \mathrm{wt}(a) \cdot \mathrm{wt}(c_0) \leq r \cdot \ell$, and so $c$ has at least $\max\{0,k-\ell \cdot r\}$ zero entries. But this means that 
$$\mathrm{wt}(c_0) + (k- \mathrm{wt}(c_1)) \geq \ell +\max\{0,k-\ell \cdot r\} = \max\{\ell,k-\ell \cdot (r-1)\}, $$
where the righthand expression is minimized when $\ell = \frac kr$, in which case it equals $\frac kr$. Finally, note that
$$\mathrm{wt}_\mathrm{bal}(c) \geq \min \left\{\mathrm{wt}(c_0) + \mathrm{wt}(c_1), \mathrm{wt}(c_0) + (k- \mathrm{wt}(c_1)) 
\right\} \geq \min \left\{\frac{d} {b} +1, \frac k r\right\}.$$




\begin{flushright} $\blacksquare$

label: lem:sidon_2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sidon_2}
Let $a=(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k) \in \{0,1\}^k$ be the indicator vector of a Sidon set $S \subseteq [k]$ of size $d$, and let $A$ be the binary $k \times k$ circulant matrix whose first column is $a$. Then $A$ is a $(d,2)$-design matrix.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $A$ is circulant and $\mathrm{wt}(a)=d$, we clearly have that each column of $A$ has weight $d$. Next we show that the intersection of the supports of any pair of columns of $A$ has size at most $2$.  


Fix $1\leq i<j \leq k$, we shall show that the intersection of the supports of the 
 $i$-th and $j$-th columns of $A$ has size at most $2$. 
 
Suppose on the contrary that  the intersection has size at least $3$. 
 
Then by the circulant structure of $A$, there exist distinct $s_1,  s_2, s_3 \in S$ and distinct $s'_1, s'_2, s'_3 \in S$ so that
\begin{equation}
    s_1+i\equiv s'_1+j, \;\;s_2+i \equiv s'_2+j, \;\;\text{and}\;\; s_3+i\equiv s'_3+j\; (\bmod \; k),
\end{equation}
or equivalently,
$$
    s_1-s'_1\equiv s_2-s'_2\equiv s_3-s'_3\equiv j-i\;(\bmod \;k).
$$
Furthermore, since $S \subseteq [k]$, we have that $-k+1\leq s_1-s'_1,s_2-s'_2,s_3-s'_3\leq k-1$, therefore they are all equal $j-i$ or $j-i-k$, since $1\leq j-i\leq k-1$. Furthermore, we have that $s_1 \neq s'_1$, $s_2 \neq s'_2$, and $s_3 \neq s'_3$.

Consequently, by the pigeonhole principle, there exist two values out of the three values $s_1-s'_1,s_2-s'_2,s_3-s'_3$ which are the same, without loss of generality, assume that  $s_1-s'_1=s_2-s'_2$. But by the definition of a Sidon set, this implies in turn that $s_1=s_2$, which contradicts the assumption that $s_1, s_2, s_3$ are all distinct.

\begin{flushright} $\blacksquare$

label: thm:cyc_to_circ
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:cyc_to_circ}
Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $I \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite sequence of integers. Suppose that there exists an explicit family of codes 
$\mathcal{C}=\{C_k\}_{k\in I}$, where $C_k \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^k$ is a cyclic code of distance $d=d(k)$ that can be decoded from $\frac d 2$ errors in time $T=T(k)$, 
and $C_k^\perp$ has distance $d^\perp=d^\perp(k)$ and can be decoded from $\frac {d^\perp} 2$ errors in time $T^\perp=T^\perp(k)$.
 
Then there exists an explicit family of codes $\mathcal{D}=\{D_k\}_{k\in I}$, where $D_k \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^{2k}$ is a double-circulant code of distance at least $d':=\min\{d, d^\perp\}$ that can be decoded from $\frac {d'} 2$ errors in time $O(T+ T^\perp+\mathrm{poly}(k, \log q))$. 
Moreover,
 if $\mathcal{C}$ is $d$-balanced, then $\mathcal{D}$ is $(2,d')$-balanced.
head: environment
name: Efficient decoding of double-circulant codes based on cyclic codes

label: cor:cyc_to_circ
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:cyc_to_circ}
Let $I := \{2^m -1 \mid m \in \mathbb{N}\}$. 
Then there exists an explicit family of codes $\mathcal{D}=\{D_k\}_{k\in I}$, where $D_k \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^{2k}$ is a double-circulant code of distance at least $d:=\Omega(\sqrt{k})$ that can be decoded from $\frac d 2$ errors  in time $\mathrm{poly}(k)$. 
Moreover, $\mathcal{D}$ is $(2,d)$-balanced.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $k=2^m -1 \in I$, let $C_k \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^k$ be the \emph{dual}  of the punctured RM code $\mathrm{RM}^*(\frac m 2, m)$.
 By   Fact \ref{fact:cyclic_dual} and Proposition \ref{prop:prm}, both $C_k = (\mathrm{RM}^*(\frac m 2, m))^\perp$ and $C_k^\perp = \mathrm{RM}^*(\frac m 2, m)$ are cyclic codes. 
By Fact \ref{fact:rm}, $C_k^\perp = \mathrm{RM}^*(\frac m 2, m)$ has distance at least $d^\perp:=2^{\frac m 2} -1= \Omega(\sqrt{k})$, and is decodable from $\frac {d^\perp} 2$-errors in time $\mathrm{poly}(k)$. Further observe that $C_k = (\mathrm{RM}^*(\frac m 2, m))^\perp$ is the code consisting of all codewords  in $\mathrm{RM}^*(\frac m 2 -1, m)$ which correspond to polynomials $f(x_1, \ldots, x_m)$ with $f(0)=0$. Therefore by Fact \ref{fact:rm},  $C_k$ has distance at least $d:=2^{m/2+1}-1 \geq \sqrt{k}$, and is decodable from $\frac d 2$ errors in time $\mathrm{poly}(k)$. 
 
Finally, we note that $C_k $ is $d$-balanced. To see this, let $c$ be a codeword in $C_k = (\mathrm{RM}^*(\frac m 2, m))^\perp$ associated with some non-zero polynomial $f(x_1, \ldots, x_m)$ of degree at most $\frac m 2-1$ which satisfies that $f(0)=0$. Then by the distance property, $c$ has weight at least $d$, and so $c$ has at least $d$ non-zero entries.  Furthermore, we have that $1-f(x_1, \ldots, x_m)$ is also a polynomial of degree at most $\frac m 2 -1$ which satisfies that $f(0)=1$, and so it is not the zero polynomial. So the codeword $\bar c \in \mathrm{RM}^*(\frac m 2 -1, m)$ associated with this polynomial has weight at least $d$. 
But this implies in turn that $c$ has at 
 least $d$ zero entries. So we have shown that any non-zero codeword in $C_k$ has at least $d$ non-zero entries, and at least $d$ zero entries, and consequently $C_k$ is $d$-balanced. 
 
The conclusion then follows by applying Theorem \ref{thm:cyc_to_circ} to the code family $\mathcal{C}$. 

\begin{flushright} $\blacksquare$

title: Remark
body_md: We could have also instantiated Theorem \ref{thm:cyc_to_circ} with BCH codes \cite{BR60}, and achieve double-circulant codes with parameters similar to those stated in Corollary \ref{cor:cyc_to_circ}. However, since dual BCH are not known to be efficiently decodable, this would not lead to efficient decoding algorithms for the resulting double-circulant codes.

title: Construction
body_md:
Fix $k \in I$, the code $D_k$ is constructed as follows.
Let $g(x) \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ be the generator polynomial for $C_k \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^k$, and note that $\deg(g(x)) < k$. Let $a \in \mathbb{F}_q^k$ be the length $k$ coefficient vector of $g(x)$, viewed as a polynomial in $(\mathbb{F}_q)_{<k}[x]$, and let $A$ be the $k \times k$ circulant matrix whose first column is $a$. Finally, let $D_k$ be a double-circulant code with generator matrix $G=\begin{pmatrix}
        I_k \\ A
    \end{pmatrix}$.

label: Dual_Check
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Dual_Check}
Let $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}^n$ be a cyclic code of dimension $k$ with generator polynomial $g(x) \in \mathbb{F}_{\leq n-k}[x]$. Then $g^\mathrm{rev}(x) \in \mathbb{F}_{\leq n-k}[x]$ is a generator polynomial for $C^\mathrm{rev}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to show that for any polynomial $f(x) \in \mathbb{F}_{<k}[x]$, 
$$
  (g(x)\cdot f(x))^\mathrm{rev} =  g^\mathrm{rev}(x)\cdot f^\mathrm{rev}(x),
$$
where we view $g(x)\cdot f(x)$ as a polynomial in $\mathbb{F}_{<n}[x]$. 

But the above follows since for any $f(x) \in \mathbb{F}_{<k}[x]$,
$$(g(x)\cdot f(x))^\mathrm{rev}  = x^{n-1} \cdot g\left(\frac 1 x\right) \cdot f\left(\frac 1 x\right) = \left(x^{n-k} \cdot g\left(\frac 1 x\right)  \right) \cdot \left(x^{k-1} \cdot f\left(\frac 1 x\right)  \right) = g^\mathrm{rev}(x)\cdot f^\mathrm{rev}(x).$$

\begin{flushright} $\blacksquare$

label: Tcirc_to_TWozen
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Tcirc_to_TWozen}
Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $I \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite sequence of primes so that $q$ is a primitive root modulo any $k \in I$.
Suppose that there exists an explicit family of codes $\mathcal{D}=\{D_k\}_{k\in I}$, where $D_k \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^{t \cdot k}$ is a $(t,d)$-balanced $t$-circulant code for $d = d(k)$. 
Then there exists an explicit family of codes $\mathcal{W}=\{W_k\}_{k \in I}$, where $W_k \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^{t \cdot (k-1)}$ is a $t$-Weldon code of distance  at least $d$. 
 
Moreover, if $\mathcal{D}$ can be decoded from $\frac d 2$ errors in time $T=T(k)$,  then $\mathcal{W}$ can be decoded from $\frac d 2$ errors in time $O(q^{t-1}\cdot (T+\mathrm{poly}(t,k, \log q))$.

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $n$ be a prime so that $q$ is a primitive root modulo $n$. 
Then if $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ is a cyclic code, then $\min\{\Delta(C), \Delta(C^\perp)\}\leq 2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition \ref{prop:primitive}, the assumption that $q$ is a primitive root modulo $n$ implies that 
$p_n(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x^i$ is an irreducible polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_q$.
Consequently, 
 $x^n-1=(x-1)\cdot p_n(x)$ is the only non-trivial way to decompose $x^n-1$. 
 
 Let $g(x), h(x)$ denote the generator and check polynomial of $C$, respectively. Then $g(x) \cdot h(x) = x^n-1$, and consequently either $g(x)$ or $h(x)$ divides $x-1$. In the case that $g(x)$ divides $x-1$, we have that either $g(x)=1$, in which case $C$ is the identity code of distance $1$, or that $g(x)=x-1$, in which case $C$ is the parity code of distance $2$. In the case that $h(x)$ divides $x-1$, we have that either $h^\mathrm{rev}(x) =1$, in which case $C^\perp$ is the identity code of distance $1$, or that $h^\mathrm{rev}(x) = -x+1$, in which case $C^\perp$ is the parity code of distance $2$. So we have that in either cases, $\min\{\Delta(C), \Delta(C^\perp)\}\leq 2$.
\begin{flushright} $\blacksquare$
head: manual

title: Proposition
body_md: Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $k,s$ be integers so that $q^s \equiv 1 \; (\bmod \; k)$. Then if $r(x)$ is an irreducible polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_q$ which divides $x^k-1$, then $\deg(r(x))\leq s$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By assumption that $q^s \equiv 1 \; (\bmod \; k)$, we have that $k \mid q^s -1$, and so $x^k -1 \mid x^{q^s-1} -1$. By assumption that $r(x) \mid x^k-1$, this implies in turn that $r(x) \mid x^{q^s-1} -1$. Next recall that the roots of $x^{q^s-1} -1$ are all elements in the multiplicative group of the field $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$. Since $r(x) \mid x^{q^s-1} -1$, the same holds for all roots of $r(x)$, and since $r(x)$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_q$, this implies in turn that $\deg(r(x))\leq s$. 
\begin{flushright} $\blacksquare$

label: conj:cyclic
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{conj:cyclic}
For any fixed prime power $q$, there does not exist an infinite family of asymptotically good cyclic codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$.
head: environment

label: prop:cyclic_conj
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:cyclic_conj}
Assuming Conjecture \ref{conj:cyclic}, for any fixed prime power $q$, and for any infinite family $\mathcal{C}=\{C_n\}_n$, where $C_n \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ is a cyclic code, we have that $\min\{\Delta(\mathcal{C}), \Delta(\mathcal{C}^\perp) \} = o(n)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let us assume by contradiction that $\min\{\Delta(\mathcal{C}), \Delta(\mathcal{C}^\perp) \} = \Omega(n)$. We know that for any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $R(C_n)+R(C_n^\perp)=1$, therefore either $R(C_n)\geq 1/2$ or $R(C_n^\perp)\geq 1/2$. But since both $C_n$ and $C_n^\perp$ are cyclic codes, 
this implies in turn the existence of an infinite family of cyclic codes of rate $ \frac 1 2$ and constant relative distance, contradicting Conjecture \ref{conj:cyclic}. 
\begin{flushright} $\blacksquare$
